report.answer_text:
TikTok briefly went dark in the U.S. in January 2025, then resumed service and stayed online while the Trump administration delayed enforcement of a federal divest-or-ban law. ByteDance signed a deal in December to give up majority control of key U.S. operations, but the deal didn’t close until January 22, 2026. (everycrsreport.com)
January–February: The Supreme Court upheld the law on January 17. TikTok went offline late January 18 as the law was about to take effect, then restored service on January 19 after President-elect Trump promised to delay enforcement. Apple and Google didn’t restore it to their U.S. app stores until February 13. (supremecourt.gov)
September–December: After several enforcement delays, Trump approved a framework on September 25 for a majority-American-owned joint venture. On December 18, TikTok and ByteDance signed binding agreements with Oracle, Silver Lake, and Abu Dhabi-based MGX. (govinfo.gov)
What changed at closing: Oracle, Silver Lake, and MGX each took 15% of the new U.S. joint venture, and ByteDance kept 19.9%. The venture took responsibility for U.S. user data, recommendation-algorithm security, and content moderation. It wasn’t a sale of TikTok globally: U.S. users remained connected to the global platform, and TikTok’s global business retained certain commercial functions, including advertising and e-commerce. (axios.com)

It will be majority-owned and controlled by United States persons and will no longer be controlled by any foreign adversary, since ByteDance Ltd. and its affiliates will own less than 20 percent of the entity

quotes.text: On January 20, 2025, I issued Executive Order 14166 (Application of Protecting Americans from Foreign Adversary Controlled Applications Act to TikTok), delaying the Act's enforcement until April 5, 2025.
On April 4, 2025, I issued Executive Order 14258 (Extending the TikTok Enforcement Delay), further delaying the Act's enforcement until June 19, 2025.
On June 19, 2025, I issued Executive Order 14310 (Further Extending the TikTok Enforcement Delay), further delaying the Act's enforcement until September 17, 2025.
Finally, on September 16, 2025, I issued Executive Order 14350 (Further Extending the TikTok Enforcement Delay), further delaying the Act's enforcement until December 16, 2025.

pages.quote_reason: The quotes show four enforcement delays issued January 20, April 4, June 19, and September 16, 2025, all before September 25, but none of the quotes mention Trump approving a TikTok framework or any September 25 approval.
pages.page_reason: The page lists a series of executive orders (14166, 14258, 14310, 14350) that each delayed the Act's enforcement before the September 25, 2025 order approving the Framework Agreement, which supports the claim that several enforcement delays occurred beforehand.
